newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong newspaper headlines - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong newspaper headlines - May 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- A "Hong Kong Free Market Index" will be launched later this month by the Hong Kong Policy Research Institute to monitor whether the territory's market remains free after the handover to Chinese rule on July 1.
-- SING TAO -- An internal Chinese Communist Party document shows that provinces have been banned from establishing administrative organisations in Hong Kong to protect the territory's autonomy.
-- U.S.-based Chinese dissident Chai Ling arrived in Hong Kong to pay a visit before it returns to China. She said she expected to return to China in five years' time.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- The government has decided to put the British and Hong Kong flags up for auction after they are replaced on July 1. It is estimated Hong Kong's colonial flag will sell for a much higher price than the British one because it will cease to exist after the handover.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- The Beijing-Kowloon "through train" set off from Beijing on Sunday morning and was due to arrive in the territory on Monday. Chinese leaders expressed the hope that the train -- the first direct Beijing-Hong Kong service -- would contribute to the territory's prosperity.

-- WEN WEI PO -- A report by China's Economic Reforms Committee said the mainland's international competitiveness ranked 26th in the world last year, ahead of South Korea, Italy and Thailand. The report was the first in China to use international standards to measure the nation's economic development.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Wine has become increasingly popular in China, with French labels holding 70 percent of the market and selling from 70 yuan to 120 yuan a bottle. But experts say the mainland market is not mature as most Chinese do not know how to appreciate wine, with some even mixing good wine with soft drinks.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The Independent Commission Against Corruption has been asked to investigate a tendering dispute involving the passenger terminal building at the new Chek Lap Kok airport.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Sources said China's biggest multi-purpose vehicle joint venture, involving German car giant Daimler-Benz, was near to foundering after two years of delays. Negotiations over the US$1 billion project were grinding to a halt due to tax uncertainties and car policy changes.
